newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs recoup early losses to end firmer in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: JGBs recoup early losses to end firmer in Tokyo.

text.p: The key March 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed firmer on Friday as persistent investor buying in cash bonds forced those who had gone short to cover their positions.
Traders said investors' buying was broadly detected in 10- and 20-year cash JGBs, even in those priced slightly over-par, throughout the day.
Earlier on Friday, the contract fell as low as 125.93 when large lot selling was triggered by a brief rise in the Nikkei stock average to above the key 18,500 level.
The key March contract closed up 0.06 at 126.35.
A total of 46.747 contracts changed hands.
The March rose to 126.40 by late morning before a substantial amount of selling kicked in.
Some traders said the steep fall was due to arbitrage selling with buying in Nikkei stock futures. But others said that the contract was hit by fresh selling.

"Many operators believe that the market is near its ceiling. So when somebody starts to sell, others follow suit," said a senior dealer at a bank's securities unit. "But they are squeezed later as they find a solid bottom -- That is what has happened in the last few days."
